title: Dan Dan Noodles
subtitle: Sichuan noodles with spiced pork mince in a sesame and chilli sauce
excerpt: The great Sichuan street noodle: wheat noodles tossed in a rich, complex sauce of tahini, chilli oil, soy sauce, and Sichuan pepper, topped with crispy spiced pork mince and blanched greens. Hot, numbing, nutty, and deeply satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dan dan noodles (dàndànmiàn) take their name from the shoulder pole (dan dan) used by itinerant vendors in Chengdu to carry their sauce and noodles through the streets. The original street version was made without the rich sesame sauce that characterises most modern restaurant preparations; the sesame sauce (using Chinese sesame paste) is a later development. Dan dan noodles are intensely flavoured: the sauce combines tahini or Chinese sesame paste, chilli oil, soy sauce, and Sichuan pepper in a balance of umami, heat, and numbing that is typical of Sichuan mala cooking. The pork topping is dry-fried with yacai (Yibin preserved vegetables) for a savoury, slightly sweet crunch; this recipe uses a substitute of pickled mustard greens or simply omits it.

content.text: Build the sauce in the bowl before adding the noodles: spoon the sauce into each individual bowl, then top with hot noodles so the residual heat warms the sauce. Mix vigorously at the table to coat the noodles evenly. The sauce should be thin enough to coat but not soupy; thin with a tablespoon of the noodle cooking water if needed.

Make the sauce: whisk together the tahini, soy sauce, chilli oil, rice vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and ground Sichuan pepper. Thin with 4 to 6 tablespoons of warm water until the sauce flows like double cream. Cook the pork mince in a little oil over high heat, breaking it up, until crispy. Add the shaoxing wine and 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and cook until absorbed.
Cook the noodles in boiling water according to the packet. Reserve a ladleful of cooking water. Drain well.

Divide the sauce between four deep bowls. Add the hot noodles on top, then the pork mince, blanched pak choi, spring onion, and peanuts. Add a splash of the noodle cooking water if the sauce needs thinning. Mix everything together vigorously and serve immediately.
